passages.title: David laments Saul and Jonathan
passages.summary: An Amalekite brings Saul’s royal objects and claims to have killed him. David orders his death, then laments Saul and Jonathan. The messenger says he killed Saul. First Samuel 31 says Saul fell on his own sword.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older Church manual says the messenger lied about killing Saul.

passages.title: Two kingdoms and the battle at Gibeon
passages.summary: Judah anoints David at Hebron. Abner installs Ishbosheth at Mahanaim. Fighting at Gibeon leads to Asahel’s death. David and Ishbosheth rule different parts of Israel. A contest between their men grows into a deadly battle.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: Why does Abner ask Joab to stop the fighting?

passages.title: Abner changes allegiance and Joab kills him
passages.summary: After conflict with Ishbosheth over Rizpah, Abner negotiates with David. Michal is returned. Joab kills Abner, and David mourns. Women’s household positions enter negotiations over power. David publicly rejects responsibility for Abner’s killing.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: What happens to Michal and her husband when David demands her return?

passages.title: Ishbosheth is murdered
passages.summary: Rechab and Baanah kill Ishbosheth and bring his head to David. David condemns them and orders their execution. Men kill Ish Bosheth to win David's favor. David rejects their act and orders their deaths.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: Why does David punish men who expect a reward for killing his rival?

passages.title: David becomes king of Israel and takes Jerusalem
passages.summary: The tribes anoint David at Hebron. He captures Jerusalem, receives help from Hiram, and fights the Philistines. Jerusalem becomes the political center. The capture account contains difficult language about a watercourse and disability. No exact entry route is established here.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me studies seeking divine guidance.

passages.title: The ark reaches Jerusalem
passages.summary: Uzzah dies during the ark’s transport. The ark stays with Obed Edom before David brings it to Jerusalem. Michal challenges David’s public conduct. David celebrates the ark’s arrival but also fears its power. His dispute with Michal divides their household.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual connects the ark’s handling with sacred responsibility. Its proposed motives are interpretations.

passages.title: Nathan announces a promised house
passages.summary: David plans a house for God. God instead promises David a lasting royal family. David’s son will build the temple. House can mean a building or a family. God’s promise links David’s family with Israel’s future.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me connects the promised house with Jesus Christ.

passages.title: Wars, tribute, and royal officials
passages.summary: The chapter collects David’s campaigns, tribute, dedicated wealth, and court officials. Joab, Zadok, and Benaiah hold named offices. War brings wealth and power to David. Defeated people face death, payments, and outside rule.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: How does David’s growing rule affect the people his armies defeat?

passages.title: Mephibosheth receives land and a place at the table
passages.summary: David seeks a surviving member of Saul’s household for Jonathan’s sake. Ziba identifies Mephibosheth, whom David brings from Machir’s house. David keeps his promise to Jonathan by helping Jonathan's son. Mephibosheth gains land and a welcome.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual studies David’s kindness to Jonathan’s son.

passages.title: Humiliated envoys and war with Ammon
passages.summary: Hanun humiliates David’s messengers. Ammon hires allies. Joab and Abishai divide their forces, and the conflict expands. David sends comfort after a king’s death. Hanun suspects a trick and shames the messengers. War follows.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: How could Hanun have tested his advisers’ claim before acting?

passages.title: David takes Bathsheba and arranges Uriah’s death
passages.summary: David sends for Bathsheba while Uriah serves at Rabbah. After she reports pregnancy, David arranges Uriah’s death through Joab. David uses royal power to take Bathsheba. He orders Uriah's death to hide what he did.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me asks readers to examine David's choices and responsibility.

passages.title: Nathan confronts David and the child dies
passages.summary: Nathan uses a story to confront David. David confesses. The unnamed infant dies, Solomon is later born, and Rabbah is taken. Nathan exposes David’s abuse of power. The child’s death also brings suffering to the household.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual compares verse 13 with the Joseph Smith Translation. That version changes Nathan’s words about David’s sin.

passages.title: Amnon assaults Tamar and Absalom takes revenge
passages.summary: Jonadab advises Amnon’s deception. Amnon rapes Tamar and expels her. Absalom later orders Amnon’s killing and flees. Tamar protests, but Amnon refuses to listen. Absalom's revenge brings another death to the family.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: What does Tamar ask Amnon to do? Who fails to protect her?

passages.title: The woman of Tekoa and Absalom’s return
passages.summary: Joab sends a wise woman to persuade David through a constructed legal appeal. Absalom returns, then later regains access to David. Joab's plan brings Absalom home. David still refuses to see his son.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: How does Joab use the woman’s story to change David’s decision?

passages.title: Absalom gathers support and David leaves Jerusalem
passages.summary: Absalom promises better justice and begins a revolt from Hebron. David leaves Jerusalem. Ittai stays with him, while Hushai returns as his agent. Claims about justice gain political force. The flight also depends on foreigners, priests, messengers, and household members.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: How does Absalom use promises of justice to win support?

passages.title: Ziba’s accusation, Shimei’s curses, and Absalom’s public act
passages.summary: Ziba accuses Mephibosheth. Shimei curses David. Hushai approaches Absalom, who follows Ahithophel’s advice concerning David’s concubines. The reader later hears Mephibosheth’s conflicting account. The concubines become targets in a public struggle over kingship.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: Whose account does David hear before giving Ziba the land?

passages.title: Hushai’s counsel and the messengers’ escape
passages.summary: Absalom rejects Ahithophel’s immediate attack plan for Hushai’s advice. Two women help messages reach David. Allies bring supplies at Mahanaim. The escape depends on people outside the royal council. Food, shelter, and risk matter alongside strategy. Ahithophel’s death remains a tragic part of the account.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: Which people bring food and other help to David’s group?

passages.title: Absalom dies and David grieves
passages.summary: David orders his commanders to deal gently with Absalom. Joab kills Absalom, and a Cushite messenger reports the outcome. David mourns his son. David's army wins, but Absalom dies. News of victory brings the king deep grief.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: Why does David’s grief differ from his soldiers’ joy over victory?

passages.title: David returns and hears competing claims
passages.summary: Joab confronts David’s withdrawal. David returns, spares Shimei, hears Mephibosheth, and offers care to Barzillai, who sends Chimham instead. Mephibosheth says Ziba deceived David. David divides the land without settling which account is true.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: Which disputes remain after David returns to rule?

passages.title: Sheba’s revolt and the wise woman of Abel
passages.summary: Sheba leads another revolt. Joab kills Amasa. A wise woman negotiates during the siege of Abel, and the townspeople kill Sheba. The woman challenges the destruction of a whole town. Her intervention saves the city, while its resolution still includes a violent death.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual states that David’s concubines were not responsible for Absalom’s violation.

passages.title: Rizpah guards the dead and warriors defend David
passages.summary: David hands seven descendants of Saul to the Gibeonites. Rizpah guards their exposed bodies. Later scenes recall battles with Philistine warriors. Rizpah guards her dead sons from birds and animals. Her care leads David to arrange burials.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual questions the executions under the law against punishing children for parents’ sins.

passages.title: David’s song of deliverance
passages.summary: David praises God through images of rescue, storm, battle, and protection. The song closely parallels Psalm 18. Poetry expresses remembered deliverance and claimed integrity. Readers should also retain the prose account’s criticism of David’s conduct.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: How does David’s song compare with his choices elsewhere in the book?

passages.title: Last words and remembered warriors
passages.summary: David’s final oracle describes righteous rule. The chapter lists warriors and recalls risky service, including the water from Bethlehem. The list honors David's warriors and their actions. It includes Uriah, whom David ordered killed.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: How do the warriors’ actions show the risks of serving a king?

passages.title: The census, plague, and Araunah’s threshing floor
passages.summary: David orders a census despite Joab’s objection. Gad announces judgment. David buys Araunah’s threshing floor and offers sacrifice after the plague. David asks why others suffer for his wrong. He buys the ground where the plague stops.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad settings only. Exact houses, battle positions, and travel paths remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older Church manual compares this account with First Chronicles 21.

guides.title: Study 2 Samuel
guides.description: Follow selected chapters through the book.

steps.title: David laments Saul and Jonathan
steps.text: An Amalekite brings Saul’s royal objects and claims to have killed him. David orders his death, then laments Saul and Jonathan. The messenger says he killed Saul. First Samuel 31 says Saul fell on his own sword.

steps.title: Amnon assaults Tamar and Absalom takes revenge
steps.text: Jonadab advises Amnon’s deception. Amnon rapes Tamar and expels her. Absalom later orders Amnon’s killing and flees. Tamar protests, but Amnon refuses to listen. Absalom's revenge brings another death to the family.

steps.title: The census, plague, and Araunah’s threshing floor
steps.text: David orders a census despite Joab’s objection. Gad announces judgment. David buys Araunah’s threshing floor and offers sacrifice after the plague. David asks why others suffer for his wrong. He buys the ground where the plague stops.

textRoutes.title: Amnon assaults Tamar and Absalom takes revenge
textRoutes.summary: Jonadab advises Amnon’s deception. Amnon rapes Tamar and expels her. Absalom later orders Amnon’s killing and flees.
textRoutes.detail: Tamar protests, but Amnon refuses to listen. Absalom's revenge brings another death to the family.

textRoutes.title: Absalom gathers support and David leaves Jerusalem
textRoutes.summary: Absalom promises better justice and begins a revolt from Hebron. David leaves Jerusalem. Ittai stays with him, while Hushai returns as his agent.
textRoutes.detail: Claims about justice gain political force. The flight also depends on foreigners, priests, messengers, and household members.

textRoutes.title: Hushai’s counsel and the messengers’ escape
textRoutes.summary: Absalom rejects Ahithophel’s immediate attack plan for Hushai’s advice. Two women help messages reach David. Allies bring supplies at Mahanaim.
textRoutes.detail: The escape depends on people outside the royal council. Food, shelter, and risk matter alongside strategy. Ahithophel’s death remains a tragic part of the account.

textRoutes.title: David returns and hears competing claims
textRoutes.summary: Joab confronts David’s withdrawal. David returns, spares Shimei, hears Mephibosheth, and offers care to Barzillai, who sends Chimham instead.
textRoutes.detail: Mephibosheth says Ziba deceived David. David divides the land without settling which account is true.

textRoutes.title: Sheba’s revolt and the wise woman of Abel
textRoutes.summary: Sheba leads another revolt. Joab kills Amasa. A wise woman negotiates during the siege of Abel, and the townspeople kill Sheba.
textRoutes.detail: The woman challenges the destruction of a whole town. Her intervention saves the city, while its resolution still includes a violent death.

textRoutes.title: Rizpah guards the dead and warriors defend David
textRoutes.summary: David hands seven descendants of Saul to the Gibeonites. Rizpah guards their exposed bodies. Later scenes recall battles with Philistine warriors.
textRoutes.detail: Rizpah guards her dead sons from birds and animals. Her care leads David to arrange burials.
